[[British Business Bank]] (8%) }} '''Bolton Wanderers Football Club''' ({{IPAc-en|audio=en-uk-Bolton.ogg|ˈ|b|oʊ|l|t|ən}} {{respell|BOHL|tən}}, abbreviated as '''BWFC''') is a professional [[association football]] club based in the [[Horwich]] area of [[Bolton]], [[Greater Manchester]], England. The club competes in the [[EFL Championship]], the second tier of the [[English football league system|English Football League]], in the [[2026–27 EFL Championship|2026–27 season]] following promotion from [[EFL League One]] via the [[EFL League One play-offs|play-offs]] in May 2026. The club started as Christ Church FC in 1874 and became Bolton Wanderers three years later in 1877. It was among the 12 founding members of the [[English Football League|Football League]] in 1888. The club won the Second Division title in the 1908–09 season and claimed the [[FA Cup]] on four occasions, winning in [[1923 FA Cup final|1923]], [[1926 FA Cup final|1926]], [[1929 FA Cup final|1929]] and [[1958 FA Cup final|1958]]. Their 1923 triumph came in the first FA Cup final held at [[Wembley Stadium]], a match later known as the "[[White Horse Final]]". Bolton were relegated from the top division in 1964 and again in 1971, but returned after winning the [[Third Division (English Football)|Third Division]] title in 1972–73 and the Second Division title in 1977–78. However, a series of subsequent relegations saw the club fall to the [[Fourth Division (English Football)|Fourth Division]] by 1987. They secured promotion from the Fourth Division in 1987–88 and won the [[EFL Trophy|Football League Trophy]] in [[1989 Associate Members' Cup final|1989]], having previously finished as runners-up in the competition in [[1986 Associate Members' Cup final|1986]]. Promotions in the 1992–93 and 1994–95 seasons saw Bolton Wanderers reach the [[Premier League]] for the first time. The club won the First Division title in 1996–97, although they were unable to retain their top-flight status for more than a single season until gaining promotion under [[Sam Allardyce]] through victory in the [[2001 Football League First Division play-off final|2001 First Division play-off final]]. Bolton subsequently spent eleven consecutive seasons in the Premier League and reached the [[2004 Football League Cup final|2004 League Cup final]], as well as the knockout stages of the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] on two occasions. Two relegations within five seasons saw the club return to [[EFL League One|League One]] by 2016. Bolton achieved promotion in the [[2016–17 EFL League One|2016–17 season]], but severe financial difficulties led to the club entering administration in 2019 after relegation back to the third tier had been confirmed. Amid the possibility of expulsion from the English Football League, the club was acquired by new ownership. Following relegation to [[EFL League Two|League Two]] in 2020, Bolton secured promotion in the [[2020–21 EFL League Two|2020–21 season]] and won the [[EFL Trophy]], for the second time, during the [[2022–23 EFL Trophy|2022–23 campaign]]. Bolton secured promotion in the [[2025-26 EFL League One|2025-26 season]] via the [[EFL League One play-offs|play-offs]]. From 1895 until 1997, Bolton Wanderers played their home matches at [[Burnden Park]] after relocating from their original ground at [[Pike's Lane]]. In 1997, the club moved to the [[Toughsheet Community Stadium|Reebok Stadium]], which has since undergone several naming changes and is currently known as the Toughsheet Community Stadium. Bolton have spent 73 seasons in the top tier of English football without winning a league title, the highest total of any club.{{Cite web |title=All Time English Top Flight Table |url=http://www.the-english-football-archive.com/records/1st_level_table.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080129141541/http://www.the-english-football-archive.com/records/1st_level_table.htm |archive-date=29 January 2008 |access-date=22 February 2008 |website=The English Football Archive}}"}}
